summary:
PASS for the scoped automated port task only. This is not full capstone acceptance. I could not execute code, so I did not re-run any acceptance checks myself.

SCOPE OF MY WORK: I read the following.
- loop/acceptance.md
- the baseline result.json, tests.log and source.json
- the coder handoff.json and process.json
- platform/doomgeneric_wasm.c
- web/index.html

I did not read platform/doom_audio.c, web/audio.js, tests/*, loop/*.py or build.sh. I cannot vouch for those files beyond the baseline logs.

EVIDENCE (paths under artifacts/runs/loop-20261105T010516Z-98b10905/):
- baseline-c802e8a5/result.json: status PASS, source_digest db7ae64a828f0aacdb7a7e34d5e5faa4d0b3dd9acb832b52d556950250c9ba25. This matches the digest in my task.
  - emcc 4.0.18 returned 0.
  - build.sh returned 0.
  - unittest discover returned 0.
- baseline-c802e8a5/tests.log: 22 tests ran, OK.
  - The audio test validated 13 MUS scores, truncation rejection and deferred audio initialization.
  - The browser test passed all of these:
    - WAD/Wasm load and rendered pixels
    - sound gesture
    - menu and new game
    - simulation pacing
    - movement, turning, and firing that consumes ammo
    - nonzero SFX and music samples
    - mute and volume
    - use-key press and release
    - synthetic blur
    - WASD, strafe and run
    - weapons and automap
    - pause and resume
    - no page, console or network errors
  - The loop fixture tests passed.
- baseline-c802e8a5/source.json: digest db7ae64a… and revision 1ba5d20.
- integration-01-3a366236/coder/handoff.json: DONE with no changes. The coder said it made no edits, ran nothing, and did not read the source. process.json shows only returncode 0 and 18.15 s. I did not treat these as proof of anything.

STATIC REVIEW:
- platform/doomgeneric_wasm.c checks for a valid IWAD and fails visibly if it is missing (:128-134).
- The ring-buffer input in dg_key rejects bad keys and drops events when full (:83).
- The BGR-to-RGBA conversion looks correct (:49-52).
- The read-only observation exports are side-effect free.
- web/index.html handles key aliases through the down map, so overlapping W/Up releases correctly (:52-69). It also releases keys on blur and when the page is hidden (:72-77), and it ignores button and input targets.
- I found no correctness or regression defect in the files I read.

RISKS (minor, not blocking):
- The baseline ran at the same digest, but this reviewer pass did not independently confirm that the tests were fresh. The tester must run a fresh verification tied to db7ae64a… before the loop counts this task as complete.
- Observation exports such as dg_in_level and dg_player_x read engine globals directly, so the tests depend on them.
- Only a synthetic blur event is tested. There is no OS-level focus test.

UNCOVERED (not established by the automated checks; do not treat as passed):
- Door and switch activation in real gameplay.
- Real OS focus transitions.
- Physical speaker output and musical fidelity. Only nonzero-sample checks exist.
- Save and config persistence across reloads. I saw no persistence layer in the files I read.
- Mouse aiming. web/index.html has no mouse handlers, and the coder said the mouse code in i_input.c is commented out. Mouse aiming is not implemented or tested.
- Manual playthrough. This has not been performed and I did not invent it.

FULL ASSIGNMENT, NOT ESTABLISHED:
- The blind teammate/instructor regression repair exercise is NOT PERFORMED. The user asked to omit it.
- Live resumption on real runs. test_loop.py covers fixtures only.
- Design rationale and reflection write-ups.
- Historical token and cost usage remains unknown.

UNRESOLVED DEFECTS: none found in the scoped port.
